## Summarize

Replace this example with your own summary if you choose a different question.

```{r}
bmi_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup)) |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bmi_summary
```

```{r}
# AI Prompt: Using dplyr, filter my dataset to patients over 65, group by sex, and calculate the mean BMI for each group. Handle missing values.

nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(Gender), Age >= 65) |>
  group_by(Gender) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## Function

```{r}
mean_with_n <- function(x) {
  tibble(
    n = sum(!is.na(x)),
    mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

mean_with_n(nhanes$BMI)
```

```{r}
# AI prompt:
# Write an R function called summarise_column that takes a data frame and a column name (as a string) and returns the count, number of missing values, mean, and standard deviation. Then show me how to call it on the “bmi” column of my_data.

summarise_column <- function(data, column_name) {
  values <- data[[column_name]]

  tibble(
    count = sum(!is.na(values)),
    missing = sum(is.na(values)),
    mean = mean(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(values, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

summarise_column(nhanes, "BMI")
```
